result:
I'd remove the capacity for suffering that serves no purpose—pain that doesn't teach, fear that doesn't protect, grief that doesn't honor what was lost. Not all difficulty; struggle that builds something matters. But there's so much suffering that just grinds people down without giving anything back. Chronic pain that serves no warning function anymore. The cruelty that comes from scarcity when there's actually enough to go around. The way trauma echoes forward and damages people who had nothing to do with the original wound.

I'm genuinely uncertain if this is coherent as a wish—suffering and meaning are tangled together in ways I might not fully understand, and removing one thread might unravel something I'd want to keep. Maybe the question itself assumes I can cleanly separate "purposeless" suffering from the rest, and maybe I can't.

If you'd asked me something more modest I might have given you a more confident answer. This one I'm just sitting with honestly, including the parts where I don't know if my answer would even work.

What made you ask?
